mechanism_narrative: A higher-than-trend FEDFUNDS rate coincides with elevated consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL), depressing real interest rates and pushing S&P 500 forward returns negative over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > FEDFUNDS_TREND for the past 2 months
regime_hint: tightening monetary policy with persistent inflation
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) when FEDFUNDS is above trend and CPIAUCSL > CPIAUCSL_TREND.

mechanism_narrative: Rising employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in unemployment (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > PAYEMS_TREND and UNRATE < UNRATE_TREND over the last 3 months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative despite consistent upward trends in PAYEMS and downward trends in UNRATE (Granger causality fails).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days as it signals expanding economic demand.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > INDPRO_M12 over the past 2 weeks
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically significant (p > 0.10) when INDPRO is above its 12-month MA.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained drop in manufacturing activity (HOUST) below trend is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days as it indicates supply-side weakness and investor risk aversion.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in >50% of periods when HOUST is below trend.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5% triggers a sharp decline in S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days as it signals recession risk and tighter financial conditions.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) when UNRATE crosses above 5%.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of increasing job openings (PAYEMS) without a corresponding decline in unemployment (UNRATE) predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days as labor market tightness improves.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > PAYEMS_prev_month for 2 consecutive months and UNRATE < UNRATE_prev_month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not positive when the labor market tightness signal is present (Granger causality fails).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) for three consecutive months predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days as lower borrowing costs boost equity valuations.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than the 30-day moving average during the cutting period.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in consumer demand proxies (RSAFS) coinciding with weak industrial production (INDPRO) predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days due to market panic about demand collapse.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < RSAFS_TREND and INDPRO < INDPRO_TREND over the last 1 week
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not negative when both demand and industrial production are below trend.
